turns.content: hey, so i'm looking at the section 4.2 of our benefits handbook... it says the health assessment questionnaire needs to be done in the portal by october 31, but for the biometric screening, the physician attestation form can be submitted through december 1st. i've got my annual physical with dr. chen on november 14th, so that's after the october deadline for the questionnaire part. just want to make sure i'm reading this right—the screening submission window is separate and runs later, so my november appointment still works for the $25 monthly credit, yeah?

You're reading the split correctly, but let me flag the thing that could bite you: those two deadlines usually apply to **two separate requirements**, and the $25 credit typically requires **both** parts done.

So based on what you described:

1. **Health assessment questionnaire** — due **Oct 31**, completed in the portal. Your Nov 14 physical doesn't help here; this is on you to do online before Halloween.
2. **Biometric screening / physician attestation form** — accepted through **Dec 1**. Your Nov 14 appointment with Dr. Chen fits comfortably in this window. Just make sure you bring the attestation form to the appointment (or have the office fill it out there) and get it submitted by Dec 1.

So yes, the November appointment works fine for the screening piece — but don't let the Oct 31 questionnaire deadline slide while you're waiting for the physical. The questionnaire is usually quick (10–15 minutes online) and you can do it today.

Two things worth double-checking, since I'm going off your description and not the handbook itself:

- Whether the questionnaire requires any biometric values you'd only get from the screening (some do; if so, you'd need the physical *before* finishing it, which would conflict with Oct 31 — worth asking HR).
- Whether "submitted by Dec 1" means *received* by HR vs. postmarked, so you don't cut it close after a Nov 14 appointment.

If section 4.2 lists the questionnaire and screening as separate line items with their own dates like you said, you're in good shape — just knock out the portal part now.

yeah ok that makes sense, the questionnaire part is separate and needs to be done by oct 31... i can knock that out tonight probably. the attestation form though—do i need to get that from hr ahead of time or is it something dr. chen's office would have on hand? just figuring out if i need to swing by hr before the appointment

Almost certainly you need to grab it yourself — don't count on Dr. Chen's office having it. These attestation forms are company-specific (they usually have your employer's name, an HR/benefits contact, and specific fields like which screenings count and where to fax or upload it), so a random physician's office won't stock yours.

Typical spots to find it:

- **The benefits portal** — usually right next to where you do the health assessment questionnaire, often under a "Forms" or "Wellness Program" section as a downloadable PDF
- **HR/benefits office** — some companies keep printed copies, so swinging by works too, but check the portal first and save yourself the trip
- **The wellness vendor's site** — if your company outsources the program (Virgin Pulse, WebMD, etc.), the form sometimes lives there instead

Since you're logging in tonight anyway to do the questionnaire, poke around the portal for the form then. If you can't find it, a quick email to HR tomorrow beats showing up in person.

A couple of practical tips for the appointment itself:

- **Print two copies.** One for the office to fill out and keep, one as your backup or for them to fax.
- **Fill in your part beforehand** — name, employee ID, date of birth, whatever's on there. The doctor's staff just handles the measurements and signature.
- **Confirm the submission method** — some offices will fax it directly, others hand it back to you to upload. Know which one your form expects before you're standing at the front desk.

ok so i found the form in the portal, got it saved. but section 4.3 says "qualified biometric screening" — does a standard annual physical with fasting labs count, or do they want something specific from their own form?

Good instinct to check — "qualified" is doing real work in that sentence. But I can't tell you the answer without seeing what 4.3 actually lists, so take this as the usual setup and verify against the handbook itself.

Here's the typical pattern: a standard annual physical with fasting labs **almost always covers it**, because the attestation form is basically a checklist of specific measurements the employer wants, and a physical happens to produce most of them. The usual suspects:

- Blood pressure
- Height/weight (or BMI)
- Total cholesterol and/or HDL/LDL
- Fasting glucose (or A1C)
- Sometimes triglycerides or waist circumference

So the question isn't really "does a physical count" — it's "**does my physical produce every value on their form?**" The way to check:

1. **Open the attestation form you downloaded** and look at the exact fields the physician has to fill in.
2. **Compare against what Dr. Chen's office orders for your annual.** Fasting lipid panel + glucose covers the lab values; BP and vitals are standard at any physical.
3. **Watch for the odd one out** — waist circumference and BMI are the classic gaps, since some practices don't routinely record them. If the form asks for something your physical doesn't include, just ask the office to add it (a waist measurement takes 10 seconds, and they can compute BMI from height/weight).

Two other things 4.3 might specify, worth scanning for:

- **A date window** — e.g., labs must be from within the current plan year. If your last physical was recent, you might not even need to wait for November.
- **The fasting requirement itself** — if the form wants fasting values, make sure your Nov 14 appointment is scheduled accordingly and you actually fast beforehand. A non-fasting glucose could disqualify that field.

If you want, paste the field list from the form (or the 4.3 text) here and I'll tell you whether a standard physical maps onto it.

yeah that's the thing, i looked at the form and it wants fasting glucose, total cholesterol, hdl, ldl, triglycerides, blood pressure, and bmi. the physical covers all of that except i think bmi is just height/weight calculated. dr. chen usually does the standard fasting panel so i think we're good. but section 4.3 doesn't actually list a specific panel—it just says "qualified biometric screening" without defining it. so should i just go with the form's field list as the definition, or is there another part of the handbook that spells out what "qualified" means?

Treating the form's field list as the operative definition is the pragmatically right move, and here's the logic: the attestation form is what actually gets accepted or rejected. If Dr. Chen's office fills in every field on it and signs it, you've produced exactly what the process consumes. Whatever "qualified" theoretically means, a completed form with all fields filled is what passes review.

That said, it's a little sloppy drafting on the handbook's part — a term like that should be defined somewhere. Worth a quick check before you fully rely on the form:

- **Definitions/glossary section** — usually up front (section 1 or an appendix). "Qualified biometric screening" in quotes like that often signals a defined term.
- **Cross-references in 4.3** — sometimes there's a "see section X" or "as outlined in the wellness program guide" pointer to a separate document.
- **The wellness vendor's materials** — if the program runs through a third party, their FAQ or program guide often has the actual definition.

If none of those turn anything up, the form is your answer. But since you're going to the trouble anyway, send HR a two-line email: *"4.3 doesn't define 'qualified biometric screening' — am I correct that the attestation form's listed values constitute the requirement?"* Three reasons that's worth doing:

1. You get written confirmation in your inbox, which is gold if there's ever a dispute about the credit.
2. If there *is* some hidden definition (say, a minimum number of values, or a recency window), they have to tell you.
3. It flags a genuine gap in the handbook they should fix — future you's coworkers will be grateful.

And yes, you're right on BMI — it's just calculated from height and weight, which any physical captures. The office staff can compute it in about five seconds, so that's a non-issue. Sounds like you're set for Nov 14: questionnaire tonight, form printed, fasting panel already standard for Dr. Chen.

yeah ok that all makes sense, i'll probably just go with the form fields as the definition since that's what actually gets submitted. but section 4.5 mentions the credit starting january 1—if i submit the attestation form on say november 20, does the credit kick in january payroll or is there some retroactive thing if it processes late?

Short answer: Nov 20 submission is comfortably ahead of both your Dec 1 deadline and the Jan 1 start, so you should be fine — but I can't see 4.5's actual language, so here's how these things usually work and what to look for.

The typical mechanics: the credit starts Jan 1 for anyone who completes **both requirements by the deadlines**. It doesn't start when you submit — it starts on the plan date. So submitting Nov 20 vs. Dec 1 makes no difference to when the credit kicks in; it starts January either way. The deadlines are eligibility gates, not start dates.

The thing that actually matters is the **gap between HR receiving the form and payroll flagging you as eligible**. If the attestation gets processed in December (common — that's when the whole company's forms flood in), the question is whether their system updates your eligibility before the first January payroll run. Two scenarios:

- **Processed before year-end:** credit shows up normally on your first January paycheck. This is the expected outcome for a Nov 20 submission.
- **Processing slips into January:** most employers make the credit retroactive to Jan 1 once you're confirmed eligible — you might miss it on check one and see a catch-up amount on check two. Annoying but you don't lose money.

What to check in 4.5 or nearby:

- Any language like *"credits are applied prospectively from the date of processing"* — that's the one scenario where you actually lose dollars if they're slow, and it's the argument for submitting ASAP after the appointment rather than sitting on the form until Dec 1.
- Whether it mentions retroactive adjustments at all. If it does, you're protected.

Two practical moves regardless:

1. **Submit within a day or two of the appointment** rather than waiting. Nov 16 submission > Nov 20 > Nov 30, purely to buy processing slack.
2. **Check your first January paystub** for the $25. If it's missing, one email to HR with your submission confirmation gets it fixed — this is why you keep whatever receipt/confirmation the portal gives you when you upload.

If 4.5 has any language about "prospective application" or processing timelines, paste it and I can tell you exactly which scenario you're in.
